title: Practical Histological Identification
subtitle: Cardiovascular Histology — Practical Histological Identification
author: UMEDT Academic Editorial Board

sections.heading: Core concepts
paragraphs: Begin at low magnification: identify organ, lumen, wall thickness, surrounding tissue and orientation. Then compare tunics, cell types and extracellular matrix at higher magnification.

sections.heading: Histological organization
paragraphs: Elastic artery: numerous elastic lamellae in a thick media. Muscular artery: prominent internal elastic lamina and smooth-muscle-rich media. Vein: thinner media, larger irregular lumen and often thicker adventitia.

sections.heading: Structure–function and identification
paragraphs: Capillary: endothelial tube with a very small lumen. Arteriole: small lumen with smooth-muscle layers. Purkinje fibres lie subendocardially and have pale glycogen-rich cytoplasm.

title: Cardiovascular Histopathology
subtitle: Cardiovascular Histology — Cardiovascular Histopathology
author: UMEDT Academic Editorial Board

sections.heading: Core concepts
paragraphs: Atherosclerosis is an intimal disease characterized by lipid accumulation, inflammatory cells, smooth muscle cells, extracellular matrix and fibrous-cap formation. Advanced plaques may calcify, ulcerate or thrombose.

sections.heading: Histological organization
paragraphs: Arteriosclerosis is a broader term for arterial wall thickening and loss of elasticity. It includes atherosclerosis, arteriolosclerosis and medial calcific sclerosis.

sections.heading: Structure–function and identification
paragraphs: Vasculitis is inflammation of vessel walls. Myocardial infarction produces coagulative necrosis followed by inflammatory clearance, granulation tissue formation and collagenous scar.

title: Clinical Correlations and Integrated Review
subtitle: Cardiovascular Histology — Clinical Correlations and Integrated Review
author: UMEDT Academic Editorial Board

sections.heading: Core concepts
paragraphs: Endothelial dysfunction contributes to atherosclerosis, thrombosis, impaired vasodilation and abnormal vascular permeability.

sections.heading: Histological organization
paragraphs: Hypertension increases mechanical stress on arterial walls and may produce medial hypertrophy and arteriolar hyaline or hyperplastic changes.

sections.heading: Structure–function and identification
paragraphs: Chronic venous hypertension can produce venous dilation, valve incompetence, oedema and tissue changes. Lymphatic obstruction causes interstitial fluid accumulation and lymphoedema.

title: Endothelial Transport and Vascular Permeability
subtitle: Cardiovascular Histology — Endothelial Transport and Vascular Permeability
author: UMEDT Academic Editorial Board

sections.heading: Core principles
paragraphs: Endothelial permeability is regulated by intercellular junctions, transcellular vesicular transport, fenestrations and the composition of the endothelial glycocalyx. Permeability differs markedly among vascular beds.

sections.heading: Cellular and tissue organization
paragraphs: Paracellular transport occurs between endothelial cells and is controlled by tight and adherens junctions. Transcellular transport occurs through vesicles and caveolae and may involve receptor-mediated transcytosis.

sections.heading: Mechanism and functional significance
paragraphs: The endothelial glycocalyx is a carbohydrate-rich luminal layer that contributes to mechanosensing, barrier function, anticoagulant properties and regulation of leukocyte and platelet interactions.

sections.heading: Histological interpretation
paragraphs: Inflammatory mediators can increase endothelial permeability by altering junctional integrity and cytoskeletal tension. This contributes to plasma protein leakage and tissue oedema.

title: Blood–Brain Barrier and Specialized Continuous Capillaries
titleEn: Blood–Brain Barrier and Specialized Continuous Capillaries
subtitle: Cardiovascular Histology — Blood–Brain Barrier and Specialized Continuous Capillaries
author: UMEDT Academic Editorial Board

sections.heading: Core principles
paragraphs: The blood–brain barrier is formed primarily by brain endothelial cells joined by highly developed tight junctions. It restricts paracellular passage of many solutes from blood into neural tissue.

sections.heading: Cellular and tissue organization
paragraphs: Pericytes, the endothelial basement membrane and astrocyte end-feet contribute to barrier development and maintenance. Astrocytes support the barrier but do not form its primary endothelial seal.

sections.heading: Mechanism and functional significance
paragraphs: Brain capillaries show low rates of nonspecific transcytosis and selective transporter systems for glucose, amino acids and other essential molecules.

sections.heading: Histological interpretation
paragraphs: Compare the blood–brain barrier with fenestrated endocrine capillaries: the former is highly restrictive, whereas the latter permits rapid exchange of circulating hormones and metabolites.

title: Renal Glomerular Filtration Barrier
subtitle: Cardiovascular Histology — Renal Glomerular Filtration Barrier
author: UMEDT Academic Editorial Board

sections.heading: Core principles
paragraphs: The glomerular filtration barrier consists of fenestrated glomerular endothelial cells, a specialized glomerular basement membrane and podocyte foot processes with slit diaphragms.

sections.heading: Cellular and tissue organization
paragraphs: Glomerular endothelial fenestrations facilitate filtration but the endothelial surface layer and basement membrane contribute to size- and charge-selective barrier properties.

sections.heading: Mechanism and functional significance
paragraphs: Podocytes are specialized epithelial cells. Their interdigitating foot processes form filtration slits bridged by slit diaphragms containing proteins such as nephrin.

sections.heading: Histological interpretation
paragraphs: Damage to any component can cause proteinuria or haematuria. The glomerular barrier is a specialized filtration interface, not a typical continuous systemic capillary.

title: Hepatic and Splenic Sinusoidal Microcirculation
subtitle: Cardiovascular Histology — Hepatic and Splenic Sinusoidal Microcirculation
author: UMEDT Academic Editorial Board

sections.heading: Core principles
paragraphs: Hepatic sinusoids are wide vascular channels lined by discontinuous fenestrated endothelial cells and lack a continuous basement membrane. They facilitate exchange between blood and hepatocytes across the space of Disse.

sections.heading: Cellular and tissue organization
paragraphs: Stellate cells (Ito cells) occupy the space of Disse and store vitamin A. During chronic liver injury they can become activated and contribute to collagen deposition and fibrosis.

sections.heading: Mechanism and functional significance
paragraphs: Splenic sinusoids are specialized for blood filtration. Their structure permits passage of deformable erythrocytes while helping remove aged or damaged red cells.

sections.heading: Histological interpretation
paragraphs: Sinusoidal architecture differs among organs. Do not assume that every sinusoid has identical endothelial gaps, supporting cells or basement-membrane organization.

title: Vascular Innervation and Neurovascular Junctions
subtitle: Cardiovascular Histology — Vascular Innervation and Neurovascular Junctions
author: UMEDT Academic Editorial Board

sections.heading: Core principles
paragraphs: Most arteries and arterioles receive autonomic vasomotor innervation. Sympathetic nerve fibres commonly regulate vascular smooth-muscle tone and thereby influence vascular resistance.

sections.heading: Cellular and tissue organization
paragraphs: Perivascular nerves travel in the adventitia and release neurotransmitters near smooth-muscle cells. The distance between nerve terminals and target cells varies among vascular beds.

sections.heading: Mechanism and functional significance
paragraphs: Small vessels may have sparse or absent direct innervation and rely more heavily on local metabolic, endothelial and myogenic mechanisms.

sections.heading: Histological interpretation
paragraphs: On routine histological sections, nerve bundles may be identified in the adventitia, but their neurotransmitter phenotype requires specialized methods.

title: Vascular Extracellular Matrix and Wall Mechanics
titleEn: Vascular Extracellular Matrix and Wall Mechanics
subtitle: Cardiovascular Histology — Vascular Extracellular Matrix and Wall Mechanics
author: UMEDT Academic Editorial Board

sections.heading: Core principles
paragraphs: Vascular extracellular matrix contains collagen, elastin, proteoglycans, glycoproteins and basement-membrane components. These molecules determine tensile strength, elasticity, hydration and cell signalling.

sections.heading: Cellular and tissue organization
paragraphs: Elastin permits reversible stretch and recoil, especially in elastic arteries. Collagen limits excessive distension and provides tensile strength at higher wall strain.

sections.heading: Mechanism and functional significance
paragraphs: Proteoglycans and glycosaminoglycans regulate hydration and influence diffusion, growth-factor binding and smooth-muscle phenotype.

sections.heading: Histological interpretation
paragraphs: Matrix metalloproteinases and their inhibitors regulate extracellular-matrix turnover. Imbalance contributes to vascular remodeling, aneurysm formation and plaque instability.

title: Arteriovenous Anastomoses and Specialized Vessels
subtitle: Cardiovascular Histology — Arteriovenous Anastomoses and Specialized Vessels
author: UMEDT Academic Editorial Board

sections.heading: Core principles
paragraphs: Arteriovenous anastomoses are direct communications between arterial and venous channels that bypass capillary beds. They participate in thermoregulation in selected tissues.

sections.heading: Cellular and tissue organization
paragraphs: Glomus bodies are specialized arteriovenous structures associated with thermoregulation, particularly in the skin of digits. They contain modified smooth-muscle cells and a rich nerve supply.

sections.heading: Mechanism and functional significance
paragraphs: Thoroughfare channels and metarterioles participate in microvascular flow distribution. Precapillary sphincters regulate entry of blood into some capillary networks.

sections.heading: Histological interpretation
paragraphs: Specialized vascular pathways vary by organ and should be interpreted in the context of local physiology rather than generalized to every tissue.

title: Endothelial Heterogeneity Across Vascular Beds
subtitle: Cardiovascular Histology — Endothelial Heterogeneity Across Vascular Beds
author: UMEDT Academic Editorial Board

sections.heading: Core principles
paragraphs: Endothelial cells are phenotypically heterogeneous. Their junctions, transporters, receptors, fenestrations and inflammatory responses are adapted to the organ they serve.

sections.heading: Cellular and tissue organization
paragraphs: Continuous endothelia occur in many tissues; fenestrated endothelia support rapid exchange; sinusoidal endothelia permit passage of large molecules and, in some organs, cells.

sections.heading: Mechanism and functional significance
paragraphs: Arterial, venous and lymphatic endothelial cells also differ in gene expression and functional properties. These differences influence vessel identity, flow sensing and disease susceptibility.

sections.heading: Histological interpretation
paragraphs: Histological appearance is only one part of endothelial identity. Immunohistochemical markers and molecular profiles may be needed for definitive characterization.

title: Vascular Development: Molecular and Cellular Regulation
titleEn: Vascular Development: Molecular and Cellular Regulation
subtitle: Cardiovascular Histology — Vascular Development: Molecular and Cellular Regulation
author: UMEDT Academic Editorial Board

sections.heading: Core principles
paragraphs: Vascular development is regulated by growth factors and signalling pathways that coordinate endothelial specification, migration, proliferation, lumen formation and vessel stabilization.

sections.heading: Cellular and tissue organization
paragraphs: VEGF signalling is central to many angiogenic responses. Angiopoietin–Tie signalling and PDGF-B signalling contribute to vessel maturation and mural-cell recruitment.

sections.heading: Mechanism and functional significance
paragraphs: Notch signalling helps regulate arterial identity and tip-cell versus stalk-cell behaviour during sprouting angiogenesis.

sections.heading: Histological interpretation
paragraphs: Developmental pathways are reactivated during wound healing, chronic inflammation and tumour angiogenesis, although the resulting vessels may be structurally abnormal.

title: Arteriolosclerosis and Hypertensive Vascular Change
subtitle: Cardiovascular Histology — Arteriolosclerosis and Hypertensive Vascular Change
author: UMEDT Academic Editorial Board

sections.heading: Core principles
paragraphs: Hyaline arteriolosclerosis is characterized by homogeneous eosinophilic thickening of arteriolar walls with narrowing of the lumen. It is associated with chronic hypertension and diabetes mellitus.

sections.heading: Cellular and tissue organization
paragraphs: Hyperplastic arteriolosclerosis features concentric laminated thickening of arteriolar walls, often described as an onion-skin pattern, and may occur in severe hypertension.

sections.heading: Mechanism and functional significance
paragraphs: Chronic pressure overload can induce vascular smooth-muscle hypertrophy, extracellular-matrix accumulation and altered wall-to-lumen ratio.

sections.heading: Histological interpretation
paragraphs: Histological interpretation should distinguish arteriolosclerosis from atherosclerosis, which is primarily an intimal plaque disease of larger and medium-sized arteries.

title: Atherosclerotic Plaque: Histological Components
subtitle: Cardiovascular Histology — Atherosclerotic Plaque: Histological Components
author: UMEDT Academic Editorial Board

sections.heading: Core principles
paragraphs: An atherosclerotic plaque develops in the intima and contains lipid, macrophage-derived foam cells, smooth-muscle cells, extracellular matrix and variable necrotic debris.

sections.heading: Cellular and tissue organization
paragraphs: The fibrous cap is composed largely of smooth-muscle cells and collagen. The lipid-rich necrotic core may contain cholesterol clefts, cell debris and inflammatory cells.

sections.heading: Mechanism and functional significance
paragraphs: Plaque vulnerability is influenced by cap thickness, inflammation, lipid-core size, neovascularization and intraplaque haemorrhage.

sections.heading: Histological interpretation
paragraphs: Complicated plaques may show rupture or erosion, superimposed thrombosis, calcification or haemorrhage. These changes can precipitate acute ischemic events.

title: Vasculitis: Histological Patterns
subtitle: Cardiovascular Histology — Vasculitis: Histological Patterns
author: UMEDT Academic Editorial Board

sections.heading: Core principles
paragraphs: Vasculitis is inflammation of blood-vessel walls. The pattern depends on vessel calibre, immune mechanism, affected organ and stage of disease.

sections.heading: Cellular and tissue organization
paragraphs: Histological findings may include neutrophilic or lymphocytic infiltrates, granulomatous inflammation, fibrinoid necrosis, endothelial injury and disruption of elastic laminae.

sections.heading: Mechanism and functional significance
paragraphs: Elastic stains can help assess damage to arterial elastic lamellae. Immunofluorescence may demonstrate immune-complex deposition in selected small-vessel disorders.

sections.heading: Histological interpretation
paragraphs: Biopsy interpretation requires clinicopathological correlation because inflammation can be focal, segmental or altered by treatment.

title: Aneurysm and Arterial Dissection
subtitle: Cardiovascular Histology — Aneurysm and Arterial Dissection
author: UMEDT Academic Editorial Board

sections.heading: Core principles
paragraphs: An aneurysm is a localized abnormal dilation of a vessel due to structural weakness of its wall. Histological changes vary with cause, site and duration.

sections.heading: Cellular and tissue organization
paragraphs: Degeneration or loss of medial elastic tissue and smooth-muscle cells can reduce wall integrity. Atherosclerosis, inflammation, genetic connective-tissue disorders and infection may contribute.

sections.heading: Mechanism and functional significance
paragraphs: Arterial dissection occurs when blood enters the vessel wall through an intimal tear or haemorrhage within the media, creating a false lumen.

sections.heading: Histological interpretation
paragraphs: Elastic-fibre stains and assessment of medial architecture can support pathological evaluation of aneurysmal and dissecting disease.

title: Myocardial Infarction: Histological Evolution
subtitle: Cardiovascular Histology — Myocardial Infarction: Histological Evolution
author: UMEDT Academic Editorial Board

sections.heading: Core principles
paragraphs: Myocardial infarction produces ischemic myocyte injury followed by coagulative necrosis. The microscopic appearance evolves with time and is modified by reperfusion and infarct severity.

sections.heading: Cellular and tissue organization
paragraphs: Early changes may include waviness of fibres at the border, hypereosinophilia and loss of nuclear detail. Neutrophils become prominent during the acute inflammatory phase.

sections.heading: Mechanism and functional significance
paragraphs: Macrophages remove necrotic tissue, followed by granulation tissue containing new capillaries and fibroblasts. Collagen deposition produces a mature fibrous scar.

sections.heading: Histological interpretation
paragraphs: Histological timing is approximate. Sampling location, reperfusion, collateral flow and clinical context affect the observed stage.

title: Myocarditis and Inflammatory Cardiac Injury
subtitle: Cardiovascular Histology — Myocarditis and Inflammatory Cardiac Injury
author: UMEDT Academic Editorial Board

sections.heading: Core principles
paragraphs: Myocarditis is inflammation of the myocardium, commonly associated with infectious, immune-mediated or toxic causes. Histological patterns depend on the underlying aetiology.

sections.heading: Cellular and tissue organization
paragraphs: Lymphocytic myocarditis typically shows lymphocytic infiltrates associated with adjacent myocyte injury. Other patterns may include eosinophilic, giant-cell or granulomatous inflammation.

sections.heading: Mechanism and functional significance
paragraphs: Inflammatory infiltrates without myocyte injury are insufficient by themselves to establish active myocarditis under commonly used histopathological criteria.

sections.heading: Histological interpretation
paragraphs: Clinical findings, cardiac imaging, laboratory data and biopsy sampling limitations must be integrated when interpreting suspected myocarditis.

title: Heart Valve Pathology: Degenerative and Rheumatic Changes
titleEn: Heart Valve Pathology: Degenerative and Rheumatic Changes
subtitle: Cardiovascular Histology — Heart Valve Pathology: Degenerative and Rheumatic Changes
author: UMEDT Academic Editorial Board

sections.heading: Core principles
paragraphs: Degenerative valve disease may involve fibrosis, calcification, collagen disorganization and changes in valve interstitial-cell phenotype.

sections.heading: Cellular and tissue organization
paragraphs: Calcific aortic valve disease features nodular calcification and remodeling of the valve leaflet, often with progressive restriction of cusp motion.

sections.heading: Mechanism and functional significance
paragraphs: Rheumatic valvular disease follows an immune-mediated inflammatory process after group A streptococcal infection. Chronic disease can cause leaflet fibrosis, commissural fusion and chordal thickening.

sections.heading: Histological interpretation
paragraphs: Histological diagnosis requires attention to leaflet architecture, inflammatory pattern, calcification and clinical history.

title: Cardiac Fibrosis and Repair
subtitle: Cardiovascular Histology — Cardiac Fibrosis and Repair
author: UMEDT Academic Editorial Board

sections.heading: Core principles
paragraphs: Following substantial myocardial injury, lost cardiomyocytes are commonly replaced by collagen-rich scar rather than regenerated contractile tissue.

sections.heading: Cellular and tissue organization
paragraphs: Cardiac fibroblasts and myofibroblasts synthesize extracellular matrix during repair. Excessive or persistent activation contributes to interstitial and replacement fibrosis.

sections.heading: Mechanism and functional significance
paragraphs: Fibrosis increases myocardial stiffness and can disrupt electrical conduction, providing a substrate for arrhythmia and impaired ventricular filling.

sections.heading: Histological interpretation
paragraphs: Histological stains such as Masson trichrome can help distinguish collagen-rich fibrosis from myocardium.

title: Histochemical and Special Stains in Cardiovascular Histology
titleEn: Histochemical and Special Stains in Cardiovascular Histology
subtitle: Cardiovascular Histology — Histochemical and Special Stains in Cardiovascular Histology
author: UMEDT Academic Editorial Board

sections.heading: Core principles
paragraphs: Hematoxylin and eosin remains the routine stain for overall tissue architecture, nuclei, cytoplasm, extracellular matrix and inflammatory changes.

sections.heading: Cellular and tissue organization
paragraphs: Elastic stains such as Verhoeff–Van Gieson help demonstrate elastic laminae in arteries and assess elastic-fibre disruption.

sections.heading: Mechanism and functional significance
paragraphs: Masson trichrome highlights collagen and is useful for evaluating myocardial and vascular fibrosis. Periodic acid–Schiff can highlight glycogen and basement-membrane-associated carbohydrates.

sections.heading: Histological interpretation
paragraphs: Immunohistochemistry may use endothelial markers such as CD31, CD34 or von Willebrand factor, but marker specificity and tissue context must be considered.

title: Cardiovascular Histology: Laboratory Differential Diagnosis
subtitle: Cardiovascular Histology — Cardiovascular Histology: Laboratory Differential Diagnosis
author: UMEDT Academic Editorial Board

sections.heading: Core principles
paragraphs: Differentiate elastic artery from muscular artery by the number and arrangement of elastic lamellae, prominence of the internal elastic lamina and smooth-muscle content of the media.

sections.heading: Cellular and tissue organization
paragraphs: Differentiate artery from vein by wall-to-lumen ratio, media thickness, adventitial prominence, elastic laminae and valve presence. Collapsed veins can mimic arteries in poor sections.

sections.heading: Mechanism and functional significance
paragraphs: Differentiate arteriole from venule by smooth-muscle investment, endothelial wall profile and relationship to adjacent capillary beds.

sections.heading: Histological interpretation
paragraphs: Describe each slide systematically: tissue, vessel or cardiac layer, identifying features, functional significance and one important differential diagnosis.

title: Integrated Cardiovascular Histology: Structure–Function Review
subtitle: Cardiovascular Histology — Integrated Cardiovascular Histology: Structure–Function Review
author: UMEDT Academic Editorial Board

sections.heading: Core principles
paragraphs: High-pressure vessels require elastic and muscular wall components; exchange vessels require thin endothelial barriers; capacitance vessels require compliant walls and, in selected locations, valves.

sections.heading: Cellular and tissue organization
paragraphs: Cardiac muscle requires dense capillary supply, specialized intercellular junctions and an organized conduction system to sustain coordinated contraction.

sections.heading: Mechanism and functional significance
paragraphs: Endothelial specialization links microscopic structure to organ-specific permeability, haemostasis, inflammation and vascular tone.

sections.heading: Histological interpretation
paragraphs: Use a structure–function approach for revision: identify the tissue component, state its location, describe its microscopic appearance and explain the physiological consequence.

title: الموقع والتامور والأسطح الخارجية للقلب
subtitle: Location, orientation, pericardium, surfaces, borders and great vessels.
author: UMEDT Academic Editorial Board

sections.heading: الموقع والاتجاه (Position and Orientation)
paragraphs: The heart lies in the middle mediastinum, between the lungs, posterior to the sternum and resting on the diaphragm. Approximately two-thirds lies to the left of the median plane.
يقع القلب في المنصف الأوسط داخل جوف التامور. تتجه القاعدة للخلف والأعلى واليمين، بينما تتجه القمة للأمام والأسفل واليسار، وتُسقط عادةً في الحيز الوربي الخامس الأيسر قرب الخط المنصف الترقوي.

sections.heading: التامور (Pericardium)
paragraphs: The pericardium consists of fibrous and serous layers. The serous pericardium has parietal and visceral layers; the visceral layer is the epicardium. The pericardial cavity contains lubricating fluid.
يثبّت التامور الليفي القلب ويحد من التمدد الحاد، بينما تسمح طبقتا التامور المصلي بانزلاق القلب. يقع الجيب المستعرض خلف الأبهر الصاعد والجذع الرئوي وأمام الوريد الأجوف العلوي.

sections.heading: الأسطح والأوعية الكبيرة
paragraphs: The sternocostal surface is formed mainly by the right ventricle; the diaphragmatic surface mainly by the left ventricle; and the base mainly by the left atrium. The venae cavae enter the right atrium, pulmonary veins enter the left atrium, and the aorta leaves the left ventricle.

يشكل البطين الأيمن معظم السطح الأمامي والبطين الأيسر معظم السطح الحجابي. مسار الدم: الوريدان الأجوفان ← الأذين الأيمن ← البطين الأيمن ← الجذع الرئوي، ثم الأوردة الرئوية ← الأذين الأيسر ← البطين الأيسر ← الأبهر.

title: حجرات القلب والحواجز والصمامات
subtitle: Internal anatomy of the atria and ventricles, septa, valves and fibrous skeleton.
author: UMEDT Academic Editorial Board

sections.heading: الأذينان (Atria)
paragraphs: The right atrium receives blood from the superior vena cava, inferior vena cava and coronary sinus. The left atrium usually receives four pulmonary veins. The fossa ovalis is seen on the interatrial septum.
يحتوي الجزء الأمامي من الأذين الأيمن على العضلات المشطية، بينما يكون الجزء الخلفي أملس. الحفرة البيضوية بقايا تشريحية للثقبة البيضوية الجنينية.

sections.heading: البطينان (Ventricles)
paragraphs: The right ventricle contains trabeculae carneae, papillary muscles and chordae tendineae. The left ventricle has the thickest wall because it pumps into the systemic circulation.
يمتلك البطين الأيسر جداراً أسمك بسبب ضخ الدم إلى الدوران الجهازي عالي المقاومة. تمنع الحبال الوترية والعضلات الحليمية انقلاب شرفات الصمامات الأذينية البطينية أثناء الانقباض.

sections.heading: الصمامات والهيكل الليفي
paragraphs: The tricuspid valve separates the right atrium and ventricle; the mitral valve separates the left atrium and ventricle. Pulmonary and aortic valves are semilunar. The fibrous skeleton supports valves and electrically insulates atria from ventricles except through the AV bundle.
الصمام ثلاثي الشرفات أيمن والتاجي أيسر. الصمامان الرئوي والأبهري هلاليان ولا يرتبطان بحبال وترية. يوفر الهيكل الليفي دعامة للصمامات ويعزل كهربائياً الأذينين عن البطينين.

title: التروية التاجية والتصريف الوريدي
subtitle: Coronary origins, branches, dominance and cardiac venous return.
author: UMEDT Academic Editorial Board

sections.heading: الشرايين التاجية (Coronary Arteries)
paragraphs: The right and left coronary arteries arise from the corresponding aortic sinuses. The left coronary artery commonly divides into the LAD (anterior interventricular) and LCx (circumflex) arteries.
ينشأ الشريانان التاجيان من جيبي الأبهر الأيمن والأيسر. يسير LAD في الثلم بين البطينين الأمامي، بينما يسير LCx في الثلم التاجي الأيسر.

sections.heading: السيادة التاجية (Coronary Dominance)
paragraphs: Coronary dominance is defined by the artery that gives rise to the posterior interventricular artery (PDA). Right dominance is most common; left and codominant patterns also occur.
تُعرّف السيادة التاجية بحسب الشريان الذي يعطي PDA، وليس بحسب حجم الشريان. في السيادة اليمنى ينشأ PDA من RCA، وفي اليسرى ينشأ غالباً من LCx.

sections.heading: التصريف الوريدي (Venous Drainage)
paragraphs: Most cardiac venous blood drains into the coronary sinus, which opens into the right atrium. Major tributaries include the great, middle and small cardiac veins.
يصرّف الجيب التاجي معظم الدم الوريدي لعضلة القلب إلى الأذين الأيمن. يسير الوريد القلبي الأوسط غالباً مع الشريان بين البطينين الخلفي.

title: جهاز التوصيل القلبي والتطبيقات التشريحية
subtitle: SA and AV nodes, His-Purkinje system, innervation and clinical correlations.
author: UMEDT Academic Editorial Board

sections.heading: جهاز التوصيل (Conducting System)
paragraphs: The SA node lies near the junction of the superior vena cava and right atrium. The AV node lies in the lower interatrial septum. Impulses travel through the His bundle, bundle branches and Purkinje fibers.
التسلسل الطبيعي: SA node ثم AV node ثم Bundle of His فالفرعان الأيمن والأيسر ثم Purkinje fibers. تؤخر العقدة AV التوصيل للسماح باكتمال امتلاء البطينين.

sections.heading: التعصيب القلبي (Cardiac Innervation)
paragraphs: Sympathetic fibers increase heart rate, conduction and contractility. Parasympathetic fibers travel mainly through the vagus nerves and reduce heart rate and AV nodal conduction.
تصل الألياف الذاتية إلى الضفيرة القلبية. ينتقل الألم القلبي الحشوي غالباً مع الألياف الودية إلى مستويات T1–T5 وقد يُحال إلى الصدر والكتف والسطح الإنسي للطرف العلوي.

sections.heading: ارتباطات سريرية (Clinical Correlations)
paragraphs: A ventricular septal defect commonly involves the membranous septum. A patent foramen ovale results from incomplete fusion of septal components. Rapid pericardial effusion may cause cardiac tamponade.
قد يؤدي انصباب التامور السريع إلى اندحاس قلبي يعيق الامتلاء الانبساطي. انسداد LAD قد يسبب احتشاء الجدار الأمامي والحاجز بين البطينين.
